name: Monolingual Basque encoders: BERnaT, BERTeus, ElhBERTeu, RoBERTa-euscrawl
links: BERnaT: arXiv:2512.03903 (Azurmendi et al.); HF collection huggingface.co/collections/HiTZ/bernat (HiTZ/BERnaT-{medium,base,large}, HiTZ/BERnaT-Standard-*, HiTZ/BERnaT-Diverse-*). BERTeus: HF ixa-ehu/berteus-base-cased; paper Agerri et al., LREC 2020 'Give your Text Representation Models some Love: the Case for Basque'. ElhBERTeu: HF orai-nlp/ElhBERTeu (and orai-nlp/ElhBERTeu-medium); paper Urbizu et al., LREC 2022 'BasqueGLUE'. RoBERTa-euscrawl: HF ixa-ehu/roberta-eus-euscrawl-base-cased, ixa-ehu/roberta-eus-euscrawl-large-cased (also -mC4 / -cc100 base variants); paper Artetxe et al., EMNLP 2022 'Does Corpus Quality Really Matter for Low-Resource Languages?' (arXiv:2203.08111). Basque NLI data: XNLIeu (github.com/hitz-zentroa/xnli-eu, NAACL 2024).
year: BERTeus 2020; ElhBERTeu 2022; RoBERTa-euscrawl 2022; BERnaT 2025 (Dec 2025 preprint, LREC 2026 / PLN submission)
license_access: All open-weight. BERnaT: Apache 2.0 (HF model card). ElhBERTeu: CC BY 4.0. RoBERTa-euscrawl: CC BY-NC 4.0 (non-commercial; fine for a shared task). BERTeus: license not stated on the model card [uncertain].
track_coverage: T3 EU only. They cannot represent English or Spanish sides properly, so they are unsuitable for T1, T2 and for T4 mixed views (except possibly as a Basque-side feature, which is not recommended).
basque_quality: Native Basque competence (these are the reference Basque encoders). XNLIeu (NAACL 2024, test accuracy, translate-train): RoBERTa-euscrawl-large 83.0 vs XLM-R-large 83.8 (zero-shot XLM-R-large 81.1, XLM-R-base 73.4); on the native test set RoBERTa-euscrawl 75.2 vs XLM-R-large 76.4. 'Lost in Variation' (CoNLL 2025, translate-train): RoBERTa-euscrawl XNLIeu 82.63 / native 73.43 / dialectal-var 72.24; BERTeus 78.15 / 68.81 / 63.67; XLM-R-large 83.42 / 75.63 / 73.21; mDeBERTa 81.42 / 72.14 / 69.77. BERnaT (Table 4, large): XNLIeu-nat 72.79 (BERnaT) / 74.93 (BERnaT-standard); XNLIeu-var 72.82 / 74.05; QNLI 72.96 / 74.23; base-size XNLIeu-nat 67.95 / 71.28; medium 66.51 / 67.31. BasqueGLUE (ElhBERTeu vs BERTeus): avg 73.71 vs 73.23, QNLI 73.84 vs 74.26, WiC 71.71 vs 70.71.
cross_lingual_robustness: Not applicable for mixed-language input: vocabularies and pretraining are Basque-only, so EN/ES sides will be poorly tokenized and not aligned with Basque semantics - expect a large gap (near-chance on semantic relations) on T4. Within T3 they are robust to Basque dialect/register variation (BERnaT specifically targets this), though PhrasIS-derived Basque will be standard translated text.
architecture: Encoder-only masked LMs used as cross-encoders ('<eu_a> </s></s> <eu_b>' -> 4-way head). BERTeus: BERT-base (cased, 12 layers) trained on 224.6M tokens (news + Wikipedia). ElhBERTeu: BERT-base cased on 575M tokens (news, Wikipedia, science, literature). RoBERTa-euscrawl: RoBERTa base/large trained on EusCrawl (12.5M docs, 423M tokens of curated Basque web). BERnaT: RoBERTa medium/base/large with 50k BPE vocab trained on latxa-corpus-v1.1 (1.22B words) plus diverse corpora (Basque social media ~188M words, historical EKC ~21M words); three variants (standard, diverse, combined).
params: BERTeus ~124M; ElhBERTeu 124M (medium variant smaller); RoBERTa-euscrawl base ~125M, large ~355M; BERnaT medium 51M, base 124M, large 355M.
compute: Trivial: all fit in 24 GB with full fine-tuning (large at bf16, batch 32); T3 train is 3042 rows so an epoch takes well under a minute on one GPU; 5-seed sweeps are cheap.
sample_efficiency: No public Basque NLI-fine-tuned checkpoints of these models were found [uncertain], so they start from MLM weights; with ~1.3k reversible source pairs, direct 4-way fine-tuning is data-starved and seed-variant (RoBERTa-large-type models are known to have occasional degenerate runs on small data). Recommended: intermediate fine-tuning on XNLIeu machine-translated train (392k MNLI-derived pairs in Basque) before DiCo, then 3-5 seeds with early stopping on dev. BERnaT authors note diverse-data pretraining helps most when fine-tuning data is scarce.
reported_results: XNLIeu (Heredia et al., NAACL 2024), accuracy, translate-train: XLM-R-large 83.8 (XNLIeuMT 79.9), RoBERTa-euscrawl 83.0 (78.6), mBERT 74.8; zero-shot XLM-R-large 81.1, XLM-R-base 73.4; native test: IXAmBERT 64.0 / XLM-R-base 65.3 / XLM-R-large 73.8 (zero-shot), RoBERTa-euscrawl 75.2 and XLM-R-large 76.4 (translate-train); generative zero-shot Latxa-7B 50.9 (XNLIeu). Lost in Variation (CoNLL 2025): RoBERTa-euscrawl 82.63 / 73.43 / 72.24, BERTeus 78.15 / 68.81 / 63.67 (XNLIeu / native / var). BERnaT-large: standard-avg 77.88, diverse-avg 73.77, overall 76.24; XNLIeu-nat 72.79. RoBERTa-euscrawl downstream (Artetxe et al.): large avg 69.0 (topic 77.6, sentiment 78.8, stance 62.9, NER 87.2, QA 38.3), base avg 66.5. BERTeus (LREC 2020): topic 76.77, sentiment 78.10, POS 97.76, NER 87.06. No phrase-level NLI or DiCo numbers exist.
pilot_dico_results: Not evaluated (the LREC 2026 pilot was English-only; best DeBERTa-v3-base 0.75 / 0.84 / 0.79).
consistency_guarantee: none (plain classifier; rely on joint decoding / antisymmetric head / consistency loss on top)
negative_other_handling: Learned as a fourth softmax class; can emit NEG for one direction of a reversible pair. Use a pair-level NEG gate and joint consistent-pair decoding; in T3 the NEG gate can also pool p(NEG) from multilingual models' EN/ES views of the same pair_id.
metric_tradeoff: On T3 alone, RoBERTa-euscrawl-large / BERnaT-large should roughly match (within ~1 point) XLM-R-large on W-F1 [uncertain], with consistency metrics driven by the decoding layer. Their value is diversity: ensembling a Basque-native encoder with multilingual encoders typically lifts W-F1 and, via pooled pair decisions, HardCons.
integration: Drop-in: AutoModelForSequenceClassification.from_pretrained(<id>, num_labels=4, id2label=ID2LABEL, label2id=LABEL2ID). RoBERTa-type models (euscrawl, BERnaT) use '</s></s>' pair separators automatically via the tokenizer; BERT-type (BERTeus, ElhBERTeu) use token_type_ids. Restrict to Track 3 configs; use the same REVERSE_PERM aggregation.
ensemble_compatibility: Yes - 4-class softmax; temperature-scale on dev before pooling with multilingual models' log-probs.
inference_cost: Negligible: seconds for the T3 test set (~4k rows x directions) on one GPU.
rules_disclosure: Disclose: open-weight, encoder-only, fine-tuned, external data (XNLIeu / MNLI translations if used for intermediate training), ensembling. Note RoBERTa-euscrawl's CC BY-NC 4.0 (non-commercial) license; BERTeus license unclear.
contamination: Pretraining corpora are Basque news/web/Wikipedia (Egunkaria, Berria, EusCrawl, CulturaX, latxa-corpus); the DiCo Basque phrases are new translations of PhrasIS (EN iSTS headlines/images), so direct overlap is unlikely, although translated news headlines could share content with Basque news crawls [uncertain]. No labels leak. The XNLIeu intermediate data is MNLI/XNLI-derived and unrelated to PhrasIS.
structural_cue_dependence: No - model uses only the two phrases; pair_id / singleton heuristics are optional decoding-layer features.
priority: P1 (RoBERTa-euscrawl-large and BERnaT-large as T3 ensemble members; skip BERTeus/ElhBERTeu, which are weaker base-size models, unless used for cheap diversity)
expected_gain: Small single-model gain over XLM-R-large on T3 (prior evidence shows parity or slight deficit on XNLIeu), but useful ensemble diversity: +0.5-2 W-F1 on T3 from adding a Basque-native encoder to a multilingual ensemble is a reasonable expectation [uncertain]. BERnaT-standard-large looks strongest on standard-text NLI (XNLIeu-nat 74.93) among the BERnaT variants; RoBERTa-euscrawl-large has the best published XNLIeu numbers among monolingual Basque encoders.
